studies.label: Within-subject laboratory experiment: scientific divergent application task
studies.cluster_se_treatment: Section 3.1 uses a Subject ID random effect. No separate team random effect or adjustment for dependence between teammates is reported. Pair-condition score aggregation, team counts, and allocation counts for condition-order sequences are not printed (PDF pp. 7-8, 11, 15-16).

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 7, Section 2.1 Participants; all participants completed every condition, PDF p. 8, Section 2.2
counts_source.quote: A total of 100 participants were recruited via an online questionnaire. Four participants were excluded for failing to follow task instructions, resulting in a final sample of 96

arms.name: Group-AI (G-AI)
arms.description: Two-person team shares a QQ Chat idea panel and takes turns contributing ideas. Each member has ChatGPT-4o and can ask a single task-related question during each of their own turns (PDF pp. 8-9, Section 2.2 and Figure 1 caption).

arms.name: Individual-AI (I-AI)
arms.description: Participant works one-on-one with ChatGPT-4o; the idea panel is private and shows only their own input (PDF pp. 8-9, Section 2.2 and Figure 1 caption).

arms.name: Human-only group (G)
arms.description: Two-person team takes turns contributing ideas in a shared QQ Chat panel; the AI interface is disabled. The human partner is the other aid (PDF pp. 8-9, Section 2.2 and Figure 1 caption).

studies.task: Generate novel applications for transparent ceramics, electronic skin, and crystal resin in scientific divergent application tasks, with material and condition order counterbalanced (PDF pp. 8, 10).

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT-4o (OpenAI)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 8, Section 2.2; the model release year is not stated

preregistration.where: No preregistration is stated in the saved manuscript; the power analysis in PDF p. 7, Section 2.1 is not a registration.
